prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of GLP-1 physiology and of the active incretin peptide that made incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: All six of us placed B019 first, but unanimity on an opening ballot is not evidence of merit, so I re-examined the case on its own terms. The chain is unusually complete: Holst's human physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action, identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, Drucker's work on proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor-mediated actions, and then drugs with large, independently confirmed effects on glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The discovery changed the research field as well as the clinic, which is what I look for when asking whether a specific discovery, rather than a career, merits the prize. The evidence is mature (a decade or more of clinical use and large randomised outcome trials) and the interpretation is stable. A single three-person physiology-to-therapy prize is the cleanest configuration available on the shortlist.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Three names cannot carry a chain this broad: Knudsen's long-acting acylated analogues are what turned the biology into a medicine, Habener (not on the supplied credit list) is plausibly relevant to the proglucagon and GLP-1 work, and Mojsov's priority is contested. If the committee wants to honour the therapy as well as the physiology, my preferred trio understates the drug-development step. There is also a risk that the prize is read as rewarding a commercial success rather than a discovery, although the underlying physiology answers much of that concern. If attribution cannot be settled with confidence, B028 (Walter, Mori) is the cleaner two-person fallback with no comparable credit dispute, at the cost of more indirect medical impact.

responses.point: Proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen for B019, crediting Knudsen with the durable acylated analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide) that carried the biology into a transformative drug class, and treating Mojsov's contribution as real but unresolved.
responses.response: I accept that Knudsen's work is decisive for the drugs that exist today and do not think it can be dismissed as merely industrial. But substituting her for Mojsov changes what the prize is for: it moves from the discovery of the active hormone and its physiology to the engineering of the pharmaceutical. Identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form is what made later analogues conceivable, and the therapeutic step has no target without it. I would keep Mojsov in the trio and treat Knudsen as the main outstanding attribution question. A disputed priority is a reason for careful diligence, not for omission. I would support a Drucker, Holst, Knudsen citation if diligence on Mojsov's priority turned out unfavourable.

responses.point: Ranks B040 third with Michael N. Hall alone, arguing that the identification of TOR in yeast is the decisive foundational step, and excludes Sabatini over unresolved credit and conduct questions.
responses.response: A single-laureate B040 is attractive scientifically, since Hall's identification of TOR and its role in growth control is the original step, and I agree that Sabatini is best left out. But I would not place it above B014 this year. Rapamycin's own discovery (Sehgal, Vezina) and the FKBP-rapamycin work of Schreiber sit directly adjacent, so crediting Hall alone could be read as overlooking neighbouring steps, and the clinical yield of mTOR inhibition has so far been narrower than the biology suggested. It is a serious candidate, but I would not put it in this year's configuration.

responses.point: Ranks B014 second and B032 third, argues that within CAR-T June and Sadelain carry the most weight, and presents Feldmann and Maini as a coherent two-person anti-TNF pair.
responses.response: I agree that June and Sadelain are the strongest part of B014 and that Eshhar's absence from the supplied names is a real gap in the historical record. On B032 I am less persuaded: the Feldmann-Maini case is clear and mature, but it is a bench-to-bedside validation of an already formulated target concept, and I find the discovery-level argument weaker than for CAR-T, where a new modality was created. I would therefore keep B014 as my first alternative, while noting that I would want to resolve whether Rosenberg belongs before settling a trio.

responses.point: Supports Drucker, Holst and Mojsov for B019, ranks B028 second, and for B014 proposes only June and Sadelain because Rosenberg's adoptive-cell-therapy work and Eshhar's omission complicate credit.
responses.response: I agree with the B019 trio and with his reading that the decisive contributions are the physiology, the active peptide and the receptor biology. On B028 I share his view that Walter and Mori are a clean pair with a well-confirmed mechanism. Where I differ is in how much weight to give indirect medical impact: the unfolded protein response is conceptually elegant, but its therapeutic consequences are still emerging, and I think that should count against it relative to CAR-T, which is why I rank B014 ahead of B028 as an alternative. Dropping Rosenberg from B014 is defensible but not obviously correct, and I would want to discuss it.

uncertainties: Whether Knudsen should replace or accompany Mojsov, and how to treat the uncredited contributions of Joel Habener, given the three-person limit.
The status of Mojsov's priority claim for identification of the active GLP-1 peptide, which I cannot verify independently from the supplied material.
Whether the citation should reward basic physiology alone or physiology through to therapy.
If B019 is set aside, how to allocate credit within B014 among June, Sadelain and Rosenberg given Eshhar's omission.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B019, B014 or B028. My own research (nuclear receptors, dopamine neuron development) is in a different area. I co-authored nuclear-receptor work with Ronald Evans, who is not credited on any shortlisted candidate. My profile lists co-authored works with Per Svenningsson and one with Abdel El Manira, but none involves a shortlisted candidate.
